findings.summary: Caption-role order is explicitly documented; treat it as a model-scoped serialization/caption structure, not a universal prompt grammar.
Tags, natural language, and mixed prompts are all supported; tag order within sections is flexible, so one global prompt-order rule is not justified.
Character identity should be paired with basic appearance; this supports per-character Character/Appearance/BINDING grouping.
Turbo uses a separate low-step/low-CFG runtime profile, so prompt examples require model/profile/runtime metadata.
Quality/negative/runtime settings are model-scoped control blocks and should remain separate from scene semantics.
Do not promote a LoRA-assisted success into evidence for base-model prompt capability without a controlled comparison.

holds: LoRA-assisted example to base-model capability generalization
tool_impact: Store model/profile/runtime metadata with prompt examples.
Keep scene semantics separate from quality/negative/model-control blocks.
Represent multi-character prompts with per-character binding groups where evidence supports it.
Keep LoRA/control/postprocess contributions as separate authority from base-model behavior.
sensitive_content_policy: Metadata-only. Sensitive examples reduced to abstract classes such as ADULT_RELATION / INTERACTION / BODY_SITE / BINDING.
